Cross-Validation for Super Greedy Forests

cv.rfsgt.Rd

Estimates the prediction error of a super greedy forest by M-fold cross-validation. Every step of training, including the variable filter and, if requested, the tuning of hcut, is repeated within each training fold. The result is an honest estimate of prediction error, free of the optimism that the OOB error of rfsgt can have. make.folds creates folds that can be reused across calls.

cv.rfsgt(formula, data, M = 10, folds = NULL, tune = FALSE,
         verbose = FALSE, fold.seeds = NULL, ...)

make.folds(n, M = 10)

# S3 method for class 'cv.rfsgt'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

formula

Model formula, as in rfsgt.

data

Data frame containing the response and the features. Missing and non-finite values are not allowed.

M

Number of folds. Ignored when folds is given.

folds

Optional fold assignment, given as the output of make.folds, as a vector of fold labels of length n, or as a list with the indices of the held-out observations in each fold. Use the same folds in different calls to compare settings on identical splits of the data. The folds used are returned.

tune

If TRUE, tune.hcut is run on each training fold and its result is used as the filter for the forest grown on that fold. A list can be given instead to pass options to tune.hcut. See Details.

verbose

Logical. Print the error of each fold as it is computed?

fold.seeds

Optional vector of positive integers, one per fold. Each fold uses its seed for both the R and the native random number generators during tuning, training and prediction, which makes repeated calls on the same folds reproducible. Cannot be combined with a seed passed in ....

...

Further arguments passed to rfsgt, such as hcut, ntree, treesize and node.restrict. samp is not allowed, because each training fold draws its own bootstrap samples.

n

Sample size, or the data frame itself.

x

Object of class cv.rfsgt.

Details

The OOB error printed by rfsgt is a quick estimate of prediction error, but it can be optimistic. The variable filter, which is on by default for hcut > 1, screens the model terms using all of the data, including the observations that are out-of-bag for a given tree. In our tests this made the OOB error too small by about 5 to 10 percent. The OOB error is also optimistic when bsf = "oob", because the out-of-bag data are then used to compare candidate splits while each tree is grown.

Cross-validation avoids both problems. The data are split into M folds. For each fold, rfsgt is run on the other M - 1 folds with the arguments given in ..., and the resulting forest predicts the held-out fold. Filtering, and the tuning of hcut when tune is used, therefore see only the training folds, and the responses of the held-out fold play no part in training. When all folds are done, every observation has exactly one held-out prediction. The cross-validated error err is the mean squared error of these predictions, and its standard error serr is computed from the M fold errors.

Because the folds can be fixed in advance, cv.rfsgt is also a good way to compare settings, for example different values of hcut, treesize or node.restrict. Running every setting on the same folds removes the variation that comes from splitting the data differently (see the examples). Currently only regression is supported.

Folds and reproducibility

make.folds assigns the observations to M folds at random and returns a list with the indices of the held-out observations in each fold. When folds is not given, cv.rfsgt calls make.folds before doing anything else, and calling set.seed() first makes the folds reproducible. To compare settings on identical splits, create the folds once and pass them to every call.

Within a fold, the results also depend on the random number generators used by tune.hcut and rfsgt. To make a run completely reproducible, give fold.seeds. Each fold then sets both the R and the native random number generators from its own seed before tuning, training and prediction.

Tuning hcut within the folds

With tune = TRUE, tune.hcut is run on each training fold, and the forest for that fold is grown with the filter it returns. What happens next depends on whether hcut is given in ....

If hcut is not given, each fold uses the hcut chosen by its own tuner. The choice of hcut is then part of what is cross-validated, and the folds can end up with different values, which are returned in hcut.

If hcut is given, every fold uses that value together with the filter the tuner found for it (see use.tune.hcut), and the search of the tuner is extended to include that value if necessary. The value each tuner would have chosen is still returned in hcut.selected.

To control the tuner, pass a list instead of TRUE. For example, tune = list(hcut = 5) sets the largest hcut the tuner considers, and other list elements are passed on to tune.hcut. Unless they are set in the list, the values of node.center and bsf given in ... are also used for tuning.

A tune.hcut object can also be passed directly as filter, without tune. The same filter is then used in every fold, and cv.rfsgt issues a warning. If the filter was tuned on the full data, it has already seen the held-out observations, and the cross-validated error is optimistic.

Errors in a fold

If a fold fails, cv.rfsgt stops with an error of class "cv.rfsgt.error". The message names the fold and the stage that failed (tune.hcut, use.tune.hcut, rfsgt or predict). The error object also contains the original error, the training and test rows of the fold, the filter, and the arguments of the failed call. Catch it with tryCatch to examine or reproduce the failure.

Value

An object of class cv.rfsgt, a list with the following components.

err

Cross-validated mean squared error over all n held-out predictions.

serr

Standard error of err, computed from the fold errors.

err.fold

Mean squared error in each fold.

hcut

The hcut used in each fold. It can differ between folds when the tuner chooses hcut.

predicted

Held-out prediction for each observation.

yvar

Response values.

yvar.names

Name of the response.

folds

List with the indices of the held-out observations in each fold.

fold.seeds

The fold seeds used, or NULL.

M

Number of folds.

n

Sample size.

tuning

The tune.hcut result for each fold, or NULL without tuning.

filter

The tune.hcut filter used by the forest of each fold, or NULL.

hcut.selected

The hcut chosen by the tuner in each fold, before any override by an hcut given in ...; NA without tuning.

hcut.requested

The hcut given in ..., or NULL.

Author

Hemant Ishwaran and Udaya B. Kogalur

See also

rfsgt, predict.rfsgt, tune.hcut

Examples


# \donttest{
## ------------------------------------------------------------
##
##  boston housing: OOB error versus cross-validated error
##
## ------------------------------------------------------------

if (requireNamespace("mlbench", quietly = TRUE)) {

data(BostonHousing, package = "mlbench")

## the OOB error is optimistic because the filter used every observation
print(rfsgt(medv ~ ., BostonHousing, hcut = 3))

## cross-validation repeats the filter inside each training fold
print(cv.rfsgt(medv ~ ., BostonHousing, hcut = 3))

## ------------------------------------------------------------
##
##  compare settings on identical folds
##
## ------------------------------------------------------------

set.seed(1)
folds <- make.folds(BostonHousing, M = 10)

## cross-validated error for hcut = 0 to 4
err <- sapply(0:4, function(h) {
  cv.rfsgt(medv ~ ., BostonHousing, folds = folds, hcut = h)$err
})
print(setNames(err, paste0("hcut=", 0:4)))

## restricted score (the default) versus ordinary evaluation of the
## lasso terminal nodes
print(c(restricted = cv.rfsgt(medv ~ ., BostonHousing, folds = folds, hcut = 3)$err,
        ordinary = cv.rfsgt(medv ~ ., BostonHousing, folds = folds, hcut = 3,
                            node.restrict = FALSE)$err))

## ------------------------------------------------------------
##
##  tune hcut inside every fold, using mtcars for speed
##
## ------------------------------------------------------------

## the tuner considers hcut up to 4, and each fold uses the value its
## tuner selects
cvt <- cv.rfsgt(mpg ~ ., mtcars, tune = list(hcut = 4), verbose = TRUE)
print(cvt)

## the hcut selected in each fold
print(cvt$hcut)

}
# }
